title: Persons Involved
subtitle: Map of connections and personal accountability: matching documents to actions.
intro: The Lagovsky case is a mechanism created by specific individuals. The section is divided into two layers: an overall map of connections and individual profiles, where an official document stands side by side with the actual action. We do not ask you to take things at face value — we invite you to compare the texts.

items.desc:
Palkin: The investor whose actions initiated the redistribution of assets.
FEZ: The enterprise that became the arena of the conflict.
Subject: A dispute over control, transformed into a criminal case.

Salikov: A participant in the procedural chain who altered the description of a key episode.
Mitrokhina: Deputy Prosecutor responsible for oversight.
Prokopenko: Deputy Prosecutor General who signed the key refusals.
Wanted notice through Interpol, extradition requests, and international verification procedures.

items.name: Palkin
items.role: Position at Russian Railways at the time of the investment.
items.doc: Open materials document an investment in FEZ of $1,270,000 and data on the average income for his position.
items.action: The question of the legal origin of these funds is not raised by the investigation and is deliberately ignored in the criminal case materials.

items.name: Salikov
items.role: Participant in the procedural chain for a specific episode.
items.doc: The case materials contain one version of the key transaction on which the charges are based.
items.action: In Salikov's personal documents, this same episode is described in fundamentally different terms. A direct comparison of these texts reveals a fundamental contradiction.

items.name: Mitrokhina
items.doc: The defense's official complaint: 5 pages of arguments and 8 points with references to specific legal violations and dates.
items.action: A formal one-line response: 'No violations found.' The contrast between the volume of documented violations and the volume of the response speaks for itself.

items.name: Prokopenko
items.doc: The official response cites a ruling of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation as the legal basis for the refusal.
items.action: A direct quotation from the cited Constitutional Court ruling contains a formulation that is directly opposite to the one used in Prokopenko's response.

summary: This section documents the personal contribution of each participant in creating the 'legal oxymoron.' We show how, through concealment of facts and substitution of meanings, a version is constructed that contradicts documentary reality.
